chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from al-Muthanna, from Zurara ibn A'yun, who said:

He said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I am amazed, may Allah rectify you, and I am truly amazed at the Qa'im; how can he be fought against despite what they see of the miracles, such as the sinking of the desert with the army, and the call that comes from the sky?' He said: 'The Satan will not let them go until he calls out as he called out for the Messenger of Allah on the day of al-Aqaba.'

key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: The Satan, the agent of misguidance
key_terms.النِّدَاءُ: The call, referring to a divine or satanic voice from the sky
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qa'im (The Raiser/Imam), referring to Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him)
key_terms.خَسْفُ الْبَيْدَاءِ: The sinking of the desert, a major sign of the Qa'im
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْعَقَبَةِ: The day of al-Aqaba, a reference to the event where Satan tried to mislead the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Why do people fight the Qa'im despite witnessing miracles?
ai.summary: Zurara ibn A'yun queries Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the paradox of the Qa'im being fought despite witnessing major miracles like the sinking of the desert (Khasf al-Bidaya) and a divine call from the sky. The Imam explains that Satan will obstruct their acceptance by mimicking the deceptive call he made against the Prophet (PBUH) at al-Aqaba, highlighting the psychological and spiritual barriers to faith even in the face of clear signs.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (29) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Ali bin al-Hasan at-Taymali from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Yousuf from al-Muthanna that Zurara bin A’yun had said:

“I said to Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as): “May Allah make you succeed! I wonder how people will fight against al-Qa’im in spite of all the miracles they will see; like the sinking of the desert with the army and the divine call that will come from the Heaven!” He said: “The Satan will not let them free until he calls out as he has called out against the Prophet (S) on the day of al-Aqaba.”
